TRAP — ext/tabs/tabs.js:34 registers the mount region from the SAME list it draws the strip from (list.forEach(name => this.regions.set(name, $panel))). Dropping ui/'s 19 components from Doc.bar() would also strip /framework/ui/table/ of its regions entry, and container() would then walk up to /framework/'s $pages and render the component over the framework sidebar. Fix: shorten the strip, re-register the regions.

ui/ is the ONLY Doc with a large child list (19). core/Page/ has 5, ext/LayoutTool/ 5, ext/catalog/ 4, core/new/ 3 — all fine as tabs. So this is a per-page override on ui/page.js, not a change to Doc.bar(): the contract at Doc.js:21 stands for every other module.

Page.class.js:214 previews() already emits a .page-previews-group heading per run of a shared group:, and the sixteen layouts already declare five — Vocabulary, Pages, Apps, Streams, Instrument. log.msg: FOUND + FIXED — Page.css's .page-previews carried grid-auto-flow: dense, and its own comment predicted the failure: 'dense can backfill the gap a heading leaves with a card from the run BELOW it. Fine in a one-column rail, which is the only consumer today.' The multi-column consumer arrived; Fit and Flex rendered above the VOCABULARY heading that owns them. Fixed in Page.css with :has(> .page-previews-group), so only a GROUPED wall loses dense and a plain wall keeps it for .two/.big backfill.

FOUND + FIXED — masonry.js measured with getBoundingClientRect(), which is VIEWPORT space, while the computed grid-auto-rows beside it is author space. ext/demo's twin zooms every pane uncapped, so the 400px pane packed at ~1.8x and left a note-sized hole under every note. offsetHeight is the fix and ext/demo/two.js's level() already documents why. Probed in a live tab: computed gridAutoRows/columnGap come back UNZOOMED, offsetHeight UNZOOMED, getBoundingClientRect ZOOMED (57 -> 102.59 at zoom 1.8).

VERIFIED numerically in an offscreen frame — packed wall at 3197px/13 columns and at 360px/1 column, zero items overflowing the rows they were given. Filters: Apps -> 7 cards + heading, Streams -> 4, search 'mail' -> Mail only, search 'mas' -> Masonry, empty search -> all 23 back. Counts on the rail (1/3/2/6/7/4 = 23) match the wall.

Two gaps closed after the first pass: the search read a card's whole textContent, so 'mail' matched Stack and Sidebar (a form's email field, a nav word) — it now reads title + description + href only. And a wall filtered to nothing was a silent blank region with the search that emptied it in the other panel — there is an empty state now.

FOUND — a wrapping flex band defaults to align-content: stretch, so a band taller than its content hands the slack to its LINES: at 400 the rail took its own line and the wall was pushed ~390px down. Only surfaces where the band is genuinely taller than its content, which is why the twin's level() is where it showed. Both masonry pages declare alignContent: start; the other 16 layouts share the idiom and are worth a look.

FOUND — ui/page.js called this.parent.previews(), correct when ext/doc bound content() to the Overview SECTION. ext/doc later bound it back to the module's own Doc, which silently made this.parent the FRAMEWORK LANDING: /framework/ui/ was drawing Start here, AI, FAQ, Core, Styles as its component wall, with nothing in the console. Pre-existing; my tab change surfaced it. ui/readme.md carried the stale trap paragraph that caused it and now records the reversal.

A Doc's four sections ARE children, so previews() on a Doc's own Overview previews its own tab strip — four extra cards on /framework/ui/. Weighed an inert marker previews() reads (RULE#8 forbids), swapping this.children around the call (mutation mid-render), and a subset argument. Verdict: Page.previews(pages = this.children) + Doc.wall(), so there is still exactly one wall mechanism. Doc.SECTIONS is now the single list bar() orders by and wall() subtracts.

Mike, mid-task: driving his live browser tabs via the site MCP is dangerous — it interrupts him and I cannot tell whether he is mid-task. Switched to headless Playwright (global install, never package.json) with a reusable probe.mjs in the session scratchpad. Saved as a memory.

VERIFIED headless at 1600 across 16 urls — every touched page plus its neighbours: 200, no pageerror, no console error, no failed request, no horizontal overflow, no .md-error, no 'Not written yet'. Widths swept on the index at 400 / 1280 / 1440 / 3440: sections correct, wall full-bleed (auto-fill leaves 3 empty tracks at 3440 because the widest section holds 7 cards), rail usable at 400.

DEFERRED and named, not silently skipped: (1) styles/layouts/doc/file/ is orphaned — six .md files nothing reads, because page.js is a plain Page with no files: list; the four new files got no doc/file entry on purpose and readme.md's Open section says so. assign.outcome:
**Landed** — [Layouts](/framework/styles/layouts/) is a browser: a filter rail (search + one row per section, with counts) beside a sectioned wall of all 23, both ext/Panel leaves in a full-bleed fill-height page. Two masonry examples: [Masonry](/framework/styles/layouts/masonry/) (CSS columns, no JS) and [Packed](/framework/styles/layouts/masonry/packed/) (order kept, ~20 lines). The index prose moved verbatim to [The layout model](/framework/styles/layouts/model/). [UI](/framework/ui/) is Overview/API/Docs/Files with its 19 components as a preview grid.

Four bugs fixed on the way, three of them pre-existing: Page.css's grid-auto-flow: dense mis-grouped every sectioned wall (its own comment predicted it); ui/'s wall drew the framework landing's children after ext/doc reversed a binding; a Doc's derived sections leaked into its own preview wall; and pack() mixed viewport-space and author-space measurements under ext/demo's zoom.
